text:
Dev Patel: Heads up — escalation from Northstar Finance (Dedicated) asking for safer rollouts / canary controls on their reserved pool. They had a latency spike during a model/runtime update last week and want staged rollout + ability to hold/rollback with audit trail. Can someone help me with current workaround + what we can commit for beta timeline?

Owen Phillips: I pulled the ticket context — they’re basically doing “pool update” today which is all-at-once. They’re asking for 5%/25%/100% + gates on p95 + 5xx + queue depth. They also want a change approval record (who approved, when).

SupportBot: (auto) Related tickets detected: SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981

Dev Patel: yup, exactly. For now what do we tell them besides “not supported”? Need something actionable.

Rachel Kim: CS side: they’re a good beta candidate if we can give them concrete guardrails. They’re also pushing on compliance (“show me approvals + audit log export”).

Miguel Santos: +1. They asked whether we can “route a small slice to new model” without touching the rest of the pool. They’re okay with Redwood operators doing it initially.

Owen Phillips: Current state: Dedicated rollouts are effectively pool-level flips. If they do it during peak it saturates queue depth fast if perf regresses.

Owen Phillips: Workaround options (none are perfect):
- Schedule the update in a low-traffic window + temporarily raise capacity headroom (if they have burst / spare GPUs)
- Clone a second pool (if contract allows) and route a subset of traffic at the app layer (they have to own the split)
- If they have multiple routes/models, pin critical routes to old version and only move non-critical first (depends on their setup)

Sean Gallagher: From SRE perspective: recommend “low traffic window + explicit monitoring + abort plan”. We can provide them a checklist: watch p95 latency, 5xx, timeout rate, and queue depth. If queue depth starts rising steadily for >5 min, revert.

Rafael Mendes: Also: if they have any autoscaling guardrail config, ensure minimum headroom. We’ve seen reserved pools hit the cliff when utilization is already 75–80% and rollout shifts add overhead.

Dev Patel: Can we do any routing-level weighted split for them today, even manually?

Lauren Bishop: Not safely, not in a supported way. We can hack around with separate pools + external routing, but inside a single Dedicated pool we don’t have first-class staged weights enforced + audited.

Marissa Cole: The staged rollout project is exactly addressing this for Dedicated pools. We should link them to the initiative but keep expectations clear: beta is operator-driven + enterprise opt-in.

Talia Benson: Timeline (rough): we’re aiming internal dogfood first, then 2–3 enterprise customers. If Northstar is interested, we can put them on the shortlist but we’ll need SRE + Security sign-off and a feature flag allowlist.

Rachel Kim: They’ll say yes to beta if we provide (a) approval workflow and (b) default gates (latency/error/queue depth) + pause behavior. They specifically called out “don’t auto-advance if metrics are missing”.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. We should message “fail-safe = pause” (not proceed). That’s a key enterprise trust item.

Dev Patel: ok can someone give me a crisp response to send?

Owen Phillips: Draft response (support-friendly):
1) Acknowledge: staged rollouts + gating not currently available for Dedicated pools.
2) Immediate mitigation: schedule change off-peak; ensure extra headroom; monitor key metrics; rollback plan.
3) Optional workaround: if they can run two Dedicated pools temporarily, they can implement a traffic split at their edge (we can help with recommended split + monitoring).
4) Roadmap: we’re actively building Dedicated staged rollouts with stage weights + gates + manual approvals + audit logs; target limited beta soon; we can nominate them.

Marissa Cole: Add link for internal tracking: <https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PM-418|PM-418 Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools>. Don’t share that link externally, but we can reference “Dedicated staged rollouts beta” by name.

Lauren Bishop: + mention what “gates” we expect in beta: p95 latency, 5xx, timeouts, GPU utilization, queue depth. And behavior: auto-hold on threshold breach; manual approve to proceed.

Rafael Mendes: Careful on promising rollback automation in first beta. We should say “pause/hold + operator-assisted rollback” initially.

Dev Patel: Good catch. I’ll frame it as “pause + operator rollback support”, with automation coming later.

Rachel Kim: For compliance: confirm audit trail is in-scope (approval events with actor identity). They asked about export — we can say “integrates with our audit log export pipeline” but don’t commit on retention specifics.

Sean Gallagher: Also suggest they tag us before the next update so oncall can watch. We can offer a “change window” with SRE monitoring if they give notice.

Dev Patel: Perfect. I’ll reply with:
- short-term operational playbook
- optional 2-pool split workaround
- beta interest + requirements capture

Dev Patel: Action items:
- Rachel/Miguel: confirm Northstar contacts + whether they can stand up a second pool temporarily
- Owen: send me the monitoring checklist text you want customer-facing
- Talia: add Northstar to beta candidate list

SupportBot: (auto) Dev Patel marked this thread as Escalation: Dedicated Rollouts

Owen Phillips: I’ll DM you the checklist + the “abort thresholds” wording. For customer-facing numbers we should avoid hard values; say “baseline + delta” (e.g., p95 +20% sustained).

Talia Benson: Will do — adding to beta shortlist doc and flagging in PM-418 notes.

Rachel Kim: I’ll follow up with their eng lead today and set expectations: operator-led beta, staged rollouts + gates + approvals, likely early access after dogfood.

Dev Patel: thanks all. I’ll close the loop on SUP-3917 with this plan and keep the ticket open for beta follow-up.
